- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +5%+ above prior high) are common; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of sentiment decay.
- For 30d horizon, avoid over-reliance on recent 18d trend; if 18d average is rising, forecast should not exceed 10% above it unless sentiment confirms breakout.
